source_text: Apelles Marcionis discipulus obiecit spatium breve tot genera animalium cibosque anni non capere. Respondetur: Moyses omni sapientia Aegyptiorum eruditus cubitum geometricum posuit — virtute cubiti solidi spatia crescunt. Ita arca totius mundi germina reparanda capere potuit.
pass_a_gloss: Apelles of-Marcion disciple objected space brief so-many kinds of-animals and-foods of-year not to-hold. It-is-answered: Moses with-all wisdom of-Egyptians trained cubit geometric placed — by-power of-cubit solid spaces grow. Thus ark of-whole world seeds to-be-restored to-hold was-able.
pass_b_english: Apelles, Marcion’s pupil, objected that so brief a space could not hold so many kinds of animals and a year’s food. The answer: Moses, [[trained in all the wisdom of the Egyptians >> Bible:Acts 7:22]], set a geometric cubit — by the solid cubit’s “power” the spaces enlarge. So the ark could hold the world’s seeds for restoration.
